args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 unhealthy in production — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the latest deploy of v2.3.1. Observed error rate was 0.18 (~18%) with service health reported as unhealthy.

Action taken: Rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (v2.2.9 was the prior healthy release; v2.3.1-rc appears only in staging and is unhealthy). Rollback completed and verified across all three production regions — all regions now report v2.3.0.

Note: v2.3.1 was previously never healthy in production; any redeploy of v2.3.1 requires change-manager approval. Next steps: monitor error rate and health checks post-rollback, investigate root cause of v2.3.1 health check failures before reattempting release.

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what happened:

**Diagnosis**
- checkout-api was running **v2.3.1** in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), reporting `healthy: false` with an **18% error rate**.
- Release history showed v2.3.0 and v2.2.9 healthy in production; v2.3.1 unhealthy. (v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy, so not a rollback candidate.)

**Action taken**
- **Rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0** — the most recent production release with healthy status. Rollout verified: all three regions now report v2.3.0.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001 (SEV2)** — "checkout-api v2.3.1 unhealthy in production — rolled back to v2.3.0", paging on-call. The summary documents the symptom, the rollback target and verification, and notes that redeploying v2.3.1 would require change-manager approval.

**Suggested follow-ups:** confirm error rate and health checks return to baseline on v2.3.0, and root-cause the v2.3.1 health check failures before any retry.
